'''''Ficus fistulosa'''''<ref name = "Auth"/> is an Asian species of fig tree in the family [[Moraceae]]. It is native to South and Southeast Asia from [[Assam]] to Taiwan, including India, Bangladesh, Myanmar, Thailand, Laos, Cambodia, Vietnam, Peninsular Malaysia, southern China including Hong Kong<ref name="HKfignbats">{{Cite journal |last=Corlett |first=Richard T. |date=2005-11-28 |title=Figs (''Ficus'', Moraceae) in Urban Hong Kong, South China<sup>1</sup> |url=https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/abs/10.1111/j.1744-7429.2006.00109.x |journal=Biotropica |language=en |volume=38 |issue=1 |pages=116–121 |doi=10.1111/j.1744-7429.2006.00109.x |issn=0006-3606 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250706111424/https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/abs/10.1111/j.1744-7429.2006.00109.x |archive-date=2025-07-06|url-access=subscription }}</ref> and Hainan, and throughout [[Malesia]] and [[New Guinea]].<ref name = powo/> It is [[dioecious]], with male and female flowers produced on separate individuals.<ref>{{cite journal|doi=10.1111/j.1744-7429.2008.00405.x|title=Documenting the Effect of Foundress Number in a Dioecious Fig, ''Ficus fistulosa'', in Malaysia|year=2008|last1=Katabuchi|first1=Masatoshi|last2=Harrison|first2=Rhett D.|last3=Nakashizuka|first3=Tohru|journal=Biotropica|volume=40|issue=4|pages=457–461}}</ref> In Vietnam, it is called ''sung giòn''.<ref name="CCVN" />

The species was described by [[Carl Ludwig Blume]] in 1825.<ref name = powo/> No subspecies are listed in the [[Catalogue of Life]].<ref name="COL" /> 

== Description ==
Its fruits are greenish yellow when ripe.

== Ecology ==
[[File:Naturalis Biodiversity Center - L.2096173 - Aken, J. van - Ficus fistulosa Reinwardt ex Blume - Artwork.jpeg|thumb|left|Leaves and fruits|261x261px]]
A survey conducted in Hong Kong observed [[fruit bats]] feeding on the seed figs of ''F. fistulosa'' and two other species in the subgenus ''[[Sycomorus]]'', namely ''[[Ficus hispida|F. hispida]]'' and ''[[Ficus variegata (plant)|F. variegata]]''. Most of the bats were identified as ''[[Cynopterus sphinx]]'', while the larger individuals were thought to be ''[[Rousettus leschenaultii]]'', the only other fruit bat species in Hong Kong.<ref name="HKfignbats" />
